reactivity_data.value:
Water: Dissolving solid NaOH in water releases heat. Mixing or diluting concentrated
NaOH solution with water can also generate significant heat.
Acids: Neutralization releases heat and may cause rapid temperature rise and
splashing.
Certain metals: NaOH can react with metals such as aluminum and zinc under suitable
conditions, potentially releasing flammable hydrogen gas.
Incompatible materials: Strong acids and certain reactive metals; other
incompatibilities depend on conditions and materials.
Hazardous reactions: Heat generation, splashing, and potentially hydrogen generation
in metal-contact scenarios.

inadvertent_mixing_hazards.value: Mixing NaOH with water is strongly exothermic (heat of dissolution/dilution). Hazards: rapid temperature rise, local boiling, splashing of hot corrosive liquid, caustic mist, and possible overpressure in a closed vessel. Severity increases with NaOH concentration and feed rate. Initiating conditions: fast water addition, wrong charging order, agitator or cooling failure, concentration above design. Controls to verify: add NaOH to water with agitation, controlled feed rates, temperature monitoring/high-temperature trip, adequate venting, compatible materials, PPE.

source.snippet: 1.5"-BL-201-PVC dosing tie-in to water cooling loop / receiver jacket. Normal: 0.15 m3/h
1.5"-BL-201-PVC dosing tie-in to water cooling loop / receiver jacket. Normal: 0.15 m3/h

causes: Upstream feed supply interruption from TK-201.
Flow control valve FCV failed closed / valve closed or signal loop lost.
Line blockage due to sediment accumulation, particulate plugging, or frozen line.
Empty upstream vessel TK-201 / loss of suction head.
consequences: Starvation and loss of feed to downstream process unit V-101.
Loss of reactant stoichiometry or cooling stream, leading to process upset or runaway thermal conditions.
Loss of production throughput and potential process shutdown.
safeguards: Flow transmitter FI-201, FT-201 with low flow alarm (FAL).
Pump suction low-pressure trip.
Periodic line inspection and operator routine monitoring.
recommendations: Confirm low flow alarm interlock trips upstream pump before deadhead overheating occurs.
Verify operating flow remains above minimum safe threshold (0.05).

causes: Partial blockage or particulate fouling in strainer/filter.
Manual valve throttled in wrong position or control valve sticking partially closed.
Reduced upstream delivery pressure.
Increased fluid viscosity at lower operating temperature.
consequences: Reduced transfer rate into V-101, causing reaction imbalance or off-spec product.
Inadequate cooling if stream provides thermal management, leading to temperature rise.
Prolonged batch cycles or level drop in downstream equipment.
safeguards: Flow indication from FI-201, FT-201.
Differential pressure gauge across pump suction strainer.
Automated flow controller (FIC) adjusting valve opening.
recommendations: Establish routine strainer differential pressure cleaning schedule.
Ensure flow does not drop below verified minimum limit of 0.05 m3/h.

causes: Flow control valve FCV failed wide open due to air supply failure or controller loop malfunction.
Upstream feed transfer pressure surge.
Pump overspeed or inadvertent start of parallel standby pump.
consequences: Downstream vessel V-101 liquid accumulation exceeding outflow, risking tank overfill and loss of containment.
Increased reaction rate causing excess heat generation exceeding exchanger cooling duty.
Piping erosion and excessive pressure drop.
safeguards: High flow alarm (FAH) on FI-201, FT-201.
High level alarm (LAH) and high-high level trip (LAHH) on destination vessel V-101.
Flow restricting orifice (FO) or control valve mechanical travel stops.
recommendations: Verify independent high-high level trip on downstream vessel initiates upstream feed isolation.
Confirm relief and cooling systems can accommodate maximum allowable flow (0.3 m3/h). Note: Design flow (0.5) is not equivalent to maximum allowable limit unless verified.

causes: Downstream pressure surge or differential pressure inversion in V-101 exceeding upstream supply pressure.
Differential pressure imbalance across interconnected process units.
Check valve failure, reverse leakage, or absence of non-return check valve (NRV).
consequences: Backflow of process chemical from V-101 into upstream vessel TK-201, causing chemical cross-contamination or inadvertent runaway reaction.
Overpressurization of lower-rated upstream piping or equipment.
Loss of process containment.
safeguards: Check valve / non-return valve (NRV) installed on pump discharge line.
Automated isolation valve (XV) closing upon pump shutdown interlock.
Differential pressure monitoring between upstream and downstream equipment.
recommendations: Verify check valve (NRV) is documented on P&ID and included in critical safety equipment inspection program.
Implement automated fast-acting shutoff valve if inadvertent mixing of backwards fluid causes toxic gas or violent exotherm.

causes: Flow control loop (FIC) hunting or improper PID tuning parameters.
Two-phase flow slugging in piping line.
Variable upstream supply header pressure.
consequences: Process instability and temperature/concentration swings in downstream units.
Level oscillations and false alarms in vessels.
Water hammer and mechanical fatigue on piping supports and instruments.
safeguards: Properly tuned PID controller dampening with anti-reset windup.
Pulsation dampeners or surge vessels.
Vortex breaker on upstream tank suction nozzle.
recommendations: Inspect controller tuning parameters and verify stable loop operation during flow rate changes.
Verify pump suction line has adequate liquid submergence to prevent air entrainment.
required_operating_limits: Allowable flow variation band (+/- % of setpoint)

causes: Upstream feed supply interruption from MX-101.
Process isolation valve inadvertently closed / valve closed.
Line blockage due to sediment accumulation, particulate plugging, or frozen line.
Empty upstream vessel MX-101 / loss of suction head.
consequences: Starvation and loss of feed to downstream process unit DV-101.
Loss of reactant stoichiometry or cooling stream, leading to process upset or runaway thermal conditions.
Loss of production throughput and potential process shutdown.
safeguards: Flow transmitter FIT-101, FIC-101 with low flow alarm (FAL).
Pump suction low-pressure trip.
Periodic line inspection and operator routine monitoring.
recommendations: Confirm low flow alarm interlock trips upstream pump before deadhead overheating occurs.
Document minimum allowable safe flow limit to enable quantitative interlock comparison.
required_operating_limits: Minimum allowable continuous flow rate (m3/h or gpm)

causes: Partial blockage or particulate fouling in strainer/filter.
Manual valve throttled in wrong position or control valve sticking partially closed.
Reduced upstream delivery pressure.
Increased fluid viscosity at lower operating temperature.
consequences: Reduced transfer rate into DV-101, causing reaction imbalance or off-spec product.
Inadequate cooling if stream provides thermal management, leading to temperature rise.
Prolonged batch cycles or level drop in downstream equipment.
safeguards: Flow indication from FIT-101, FIC-101.
Differential pressure gauge across pump suction strainer.
Automated flow controller (FIC) adjusting valve opening.
recommendations: Establish routine strainer differential pressure cleaning schedule.
Document minimum allowable flow rate for process safety baseline.

causes: Bypass valve inadvertently opened.
Upstream feed transfer pressure surge.
Pump overspeed or inadvertent start of parallel standby pump.
consequences: Downstream vessel DV-101 liquid accumulation exceeding outflow, risking tank overfill and loss of containment.
Increased reaction rate causing excess heat generation exceeding exchanger cooling duty.
Piping erosion and excessive pressure drop.
safeguards: High flow alarm (FAH) on FIT-101, FIC-101.
High level alarm (LAH) and high-high level trip (LAHH) on destination vessel DV-101.
Flow restricting orifice (FO) or control valve mechanical travel stops.
recommendations: Verify independent high-high level trip on downstream vessel initiates upstream feed isolation.
Establish and verify maximum allowable flow rate based on downstream vessel venting and relief capacity.
required_operating_limits: Maximum allowable operating flow limit (distinguished from equipment design flow)

causes: Downstream pressure surge or differential pressure inversion in DV-101 exceeding upstream supply pressure.
Differential pressure imbalance across interconnected process units.
Check valve failure, reverse leakage, or absence of non-return check valve (NRV).
consequences: Backflow of process chemical from DV-101 into upstream vessel MX-101, causing chemical cross-contamination or inadvertent runaway reaction.
Overpressurization of lower-rated upstream piping or equipment.
Loss of process containment.
safeguards: Check valve / non-return valve (NRV) installed on pump discharge line.
Automated isolation valve (XV) closing upon pump shutdown interlock.
Differential pressure monitoring between upstream and downstream equipment.
recommendations: Verify check valve (NRV) is documented on P&ID and included in critical safety equipment inspection program.
Implement automated fast-acting shutoff valve if inadvertent mixing of backwards fluid causes toxic gas or violent exotherm.

causes: Intermittent valve manipulation.
Two-phase flow slugging in piping line.
Variable upstream supply header pressure.
consequences: Process instability and temperature/concentration swings in downstream units.
Level oscillations and false alarms in vessels.
Water hammer and mechanical fatigue on piping supports and instruments.
safeguards: Properly tuned PID controller dampening with anti-reset windup.
Pulsation dampeners or surge vessels.
Vortex breaker on upstream tank suction nozzle.
recommendations: Inspect controller tuning parameters and verify stable loop operation during flow rate changes.
Verify pump suction line has adequate liquid submergence to prevent air entrainment.
required_operating_limits: Allowable flow variation band (+/- % of setpoint)

causes: Transfer pump P-101 electrical trip, motor burnout, or mechanical failure.
Process isolation valve inadvertently closed / valve closed.
Line blockage due to sediment accumulation, particulate plugging, or frozen line.
Empty upstream vessel P-101 / loss of suction head.
consequences: Pump P-101 deadheading against closed discharge, leading to liquid overheating, seal failure, or casing overpressure.
Loss of reactant stoichiometry or cooling stream, leading to process upset or runaway thermal conditions.
Loss of production throughput and potential process shutdown.
safeguards: Flow transmitter FIT-101, FIC-101 with low flow alarm (FAL).
Pump minimum flow bypass recirculation line and motor thermal overload protection.
Periodic line inspection and operator routine monitoring.
recommendations: Confirm low flow alarm interlock trips upstream pump before deadhead overheating occurs.
Document minimum allowable safe flow limit to enable quantitative interlock comparison.
required_operating_limits: Minimum allowable continuous flow rate (m3/h or gpm)

causes: Partial blockage or particulate fouling in strainer/filter.
Manual valve throttled in wrong position or control valve sticking partially closed.
Pump P-101 impeller wear, low NPSH available, or partial cavitation.
Increased fluid viscosity at lower operating temperature.
consequences: Reduced transfer rate into MX-101, causing reaction imbalance or off-spec product.
Inadequate cooling if stream provides thermal management, leading to temperature rise.
Prolonged batch cycles or level drop in downstream equipment.
safeguards: Flow indication from FIT-101, FIC-101.
Differential pressure gauge across pump suction strainer.
Automated flow controller (FIC) adjusting valve opening.
recommendations: Establish routine strainer differential pressure cleaning schedule.
Document minimum allowable flow rate for process safety baseline.

causes: Bypass valve inadvertently opened.
Upstream feed transfer pressure surge.
Pump overspeed or inadvertent start of parallel standby pump.
consequences: Downstream vessel MX-101 liquid accumulation exceeding outflow, risking tank overfill and loss of containment.
Increased reaction rate causing excess heat generation exceeding exchanger cooling duty.
Piping erosion and excessive pressure drop.
safeguards: High flow alarm (FAH) on FIT-101, FIC-101.
High level alarm (LAH) and high-high level trip (LAHH) on destination vessel MX-101.
Flow restricting orifice (FO) or control valve mechanical travel stops.
recommendations: Verify independent high-high level trip on downstream vessel initiates upstream feed isolation.
Establish and verify maximum allowable flow rate based on downstream vessel venting and relief capacity.
required_operating_limits: Maximum allowable operating flow limit (distinguished from equipment design flow)

causes: Downstream pressure surge or differential pressure inversion in MX-101 exceeding upstream supply pressure.
Pump P-101 tripping while discharge line remains under pressure.
Check valve failure, reverse leakage, or absence of non-return check valve (NRV).
consequences: Backflow of process chemical from MX-101 into upstream vessel P-101, causing chemical cross-contamination or inadvertent runaway reaction.
Overpressurization of lower-rated upstream piping or equipment.
Reverse rotation and catastrophic mechanical damage to pump P-101.
safeguards: Check valve / non-return valve (NRV) installed on pump discharge line.
Automated isolation valve (XV) closing upon pump shutdown interlock.
Differential pressure monitoring between upstream and downstream equipment.
recommendations: Verify check valve (NRV) is documented on P&ID and included in critical safety equipment inspection program.
Implement automated fast-acting shutoff valve if inadvertent mixing of backwards fluid causes toxic gas or violent exotherm.

causes: Intermittent valve manipulation.
Two-phase flow slugging in piping line.
Pump P-101 suction vortexing, low NPSH margin, or intermittent air ingress.
consequences: Process instability and temperature/concentration swings in downstream units.
Level oscillations and false alarms in vessels.
Water hammer and mechanical fatigue on piping supports and instruments.
safeguards: Properly tuned PID controller dampening with anti-reset windup.
Pulsation dampeners or surge vessels.
Vortex breaker on upstream tank suction nozzle.
recommendations: Inspect controller tuning parameters and verify stable loop operation during flow rate changes.
Verify pump suction line has adequate liquid submergence to prevent air entrainment.
required_operating_limits: Allowable flow variation band (+/- % of setpoint)

Flow restricting orifice (FO) or control valve mechanical travel stops.
recommendations: Verify independent high-high level trip on downstream vessel initiates upstream feed isolation.
Establish and verify maximum allowable flow rate based on downstream vessel venting and relief capacity.
required_operating_limits: Maximum allowable operating flow limit (distinguished from equipment design flow)

causes: Downstream pressure surge or differential pressure inversion in TK-102 exceeding upstream supply pressure.
Differential pressure imbalance across interconnected process units.
Check valve failure, reverse leakage, or absence of non-return check valve (NRV).
consequences: Backflow of process chemical from TK-102 into upstream vessel HV-103, causing chemical cross-contamination or inadvertent runaway reaction.
Overpressurization of lower-rated upstream piping or equipment.
Loss of process containment.
safeguards: Check valve / non-return valve (NRV) installed on pump discharge line.
Automated isolation valve (XV) closing upon pump shutdown interlock.
Differential pressure monitoring between upstream and downstream equipment.
recommendations: Verify check valve (NRV) is documented on P&ID and included in critical safety equipment inspection program.
Implement automated fast-acting shutoff valve if inadvertent mixing of backwards fluid causes toxic gas or violent exotherm.

causes: Intermittent valve manipulation.
Two-phase flow slugging in piping line.
Variable upstream supply header pressure.
consequences: Process instability and temperature/concentration swings in downstream units.
Level oscillations and false alarms in vessels.
Water hammer and mechanical fatigue on piping supports and instruments.
safeguards: Properly tuned PID controller dampening with anti-reset windup.
Pulsation dampeners or surge vessels.
Vortex breaker on upstream tank suction nozzle.
recommendations: Inspect controller tuning parameters and verify stable loop operation during flow rate changes.
Verify pump suction line has adequate liquid submergence to prevent air entrainment.

causes: Upstream feed supply interruption from TK-102.

Empty upstream vessel TK-102 / loss of suction head.
consequences: Starvation and loss of feed to downstream process unit HV-104.
Loss of reactant stoichiometry or cooling stream, leading to process upset or runaway thermal conditions.
Loss of production throughput and potential process shutdown.
safeguards: Flow transmitter FIT-101, FIC-101 with low flow alarm (FAL).
Pump suction low-pressure trip.
Periodic line inspection and operator routine monitoring.
recommendations: Confirm low flow alarm interlock trips upstream pump before deadhead overheating occurs.
Document minimum allowable safe flow limit to enable quantitative interlock comparison.
required_operating_limits: Minimum allowable continuous flow rate (m3/h or gpm)

causes: Partial blockage or particulate fouling in strainer/filter.

consequences: Reduced transfer rate into HV-104, causing reaction imbalance or off-spec product.

safeguards: Flow indication from FIT-101, FIC-101.

Automated flow controller (FIC) adjusting valve opening.
recommendations: Establish routine strainer differential pressure cleaning schedule.
Document minimum allowable flow rate for process safety baseline.
